This is the indication that I have. If it's not correct, you can please feel free to make whatever adjustments you wish. Yes, Ms. Nikolic, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will not have any questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. So Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Celanovic.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I would just like to see 6D17 on the e-court system, and while I'm putting the questions, if possible, I would like to also have the English version, page 3, paragraph 3. And the B/C/S version would be page 3, paragraph 6. While we're waiting, Mr. Celanovic, I wanted to ask you the following: You recall on the 28th of August, 2003 you gave a statement at the premises of the Bratunac police station to the public security centre in Bijeljina. Was that so?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Amongst other things I'm going to read a passage to you from that statement and I would just like you to confirm it. In the B/C/S version it's in the middle of this document, which is on the right. And it says, "In the morning on the 12th of July."

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in the English version it's page 3, paragraph 1. Or actually, the third paragraph in the middle of it. It says, "In the morning on the 12th of July."

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see that, Mr. Celanovic?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It says that on the 12th of July, together with Momir Nikolic you went to the Zuti Most check-point where there was a telephone line with the UNPROFOR base outside Potocari, and that on that occasion Nikolic spoke with the members of the Dutch battalion from that check-point. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please clarify the following: On the 12th of July when you got there what time of the day was it?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: When I got there?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Together with Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: In the morning. I really don't know what time it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that the check-point still existed then and that members of the Dutch battalion were still there at Zuti Most?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I cannot agree with that. It was not like that. The check-point did exist. That was the check-point where the convoys were inspected. The convoys of humanitarian aid that were going for -- to Srebrenica. That's where they were inspected. But there was a direct line to the UNPROFOR base that was farther away. That was not the UNPROFOR check-point; it was a check-point of the military police. And then further away, two, three or 500 metres away was the UNPROFOR check-point. That's where the UNPROFOR was. He spoke with someone.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would we agree that the check-point that you are talking about is the check-point called, "the check-point at Jovo's"? Colloquially they called it that after the man who worked there.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't hear that, but I know that the check-point where the humanitarian aid convoys were checked was a place where Professor Jovo worked. I mean I -- I can't remember his last name, but it's possible that that's the same one.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And you are sure that that was when the UN or the UNPROFOR check-point was contacted?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: He said that he wanted to talk to them. I stayed outside of the container, he went inside, and carried out the conversation. He said he wanted to talk to them. I didn't hear the conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And from the place where you were, were you able to see the existence of the check-point at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was some kind of fortification, there were a lot of sandbags piled up around the building where they were. And you could see behind the bend, around the bend, there was some kind of barrier, a purely military barrier. Bags with two or three rifle nests and a couple of towers.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The next thing I would like to ask you, and I would just like to stay with the same document, but just move to page 4 of the English version, paragraph 2. And page 4 of the B/C/S version. Thank you. Mr. Celanovic, today the Prosecutor asked you to describe the people you described as specials who came with five or six people of Muslim ethnicity. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the statement that you gave you said, "amongst other things, that these were members of -- of a unit unknown to me, and I think that they were members of a special unit, judging by their weapons and equipment and they all wore black fatigues and had automatic weapons." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't see it here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The -- the question implies that that is the same unit that I was talking about, and -- and actually that does not appear from this statement to be the case from his statement. That can be cleared up, but I don't think we should have an assumption unless it is a true fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The witness says that he doesn't see it there in any case. Perhaps now that he has heard your remarks if you wish to add anything, Witness, then please feel free to go ahead. Otherwise, we move to the next question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you are discussing the uniforms, most of them had black overalls. Or maybe dark blue. It was a dark colour. And then there were a couple of them with camouflage uniforms, to be more specific. I mean when I say camouflage, I mean multi-coloured ones, if that's what you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That's all I wanted to ask you about, members of special forces, and I won't have any more questions about them. Now the next topic. Mr. Celanovic, the next matter that I want to turn attention to is the moment when Momir Nikolic arrived with Resid Sinanovic, and when you talked to Resid. Will you please tell us, did any of them tell you where they had come from.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: No. Later on Resid told me that Momir Nikolic got him somewhere near Kravica, I'm not exactly sure where, that he brought him from there in his own vehicle, but Momir told me nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did Resid tell you whether he had surrendered or was captured?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: I think this is what he told me, that he reported to a check-point in Pobudje or in another place. These are the villages in the Kravica area, and that's what he said, that he reported to that check-point. That's what he said, which I think implies that he surrendered there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did he mention Konjevic Polje on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could we now see Defence exhibit 4D14, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, once again, this is 4D16 for the sake of the transcript. This is the plea agreement and factual agreement or agreement on the facts provided by Momir Nikolic that we had opportunity to see here. Let me just give you the reference, namely we need to see page 5 of the English version, paragraph 1. And in the B/C/S version it's page 5, paragraph 2. Thank you. I think that's what we wanted to see. Now, Your Honours, and Mr. Celanovic, would you please look at the last sentence of the first passage, first paragraph in the English version, where Momir Nikolic says, Mr. Celanovic, that upon fetching Resid Sinanovic from Konjevic Polje, on his way towards Bratunac he reached the Bratunac brigade and handed over Sinanovic to the military police at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters specifically to a legal officer Zlatan Celanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My question is based on what you know, is it true what Momir Nikolic said?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, he didn't hand him over to me. He brought him to the office. I wasn't duty-bound to take over anyone. He simply brought him into the office and left him there. He didn't hand him over to me. He just left him there. I don't know how people interpret this, but it wasn't my duty to take over people. But what he said here is true. Namely, he did bring him to my office.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you then confirm and tell us that it was possible that Momir Nikolic took over Resid Sinanovic in Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't confirm that. You mean that Momir Nikolic took him over in Konjevic Polje? I don't know. I don't know about that. He brought him to Bratunac to my office.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's try to get to the bottom of this. Can we see the previous page, page 4, please? Same text in both versions. Last paragraph, please. Would you please look at it? My question is, Mr. Celanovic, do you believe it possible, do you believe it was possible that what Momir Nikolic said was true? Namely that he, Momir Nikolic, took over Resid Sinanovic in Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's possible. If that's what he says, that he took him over there, then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection to the form of the question. Anything is possible. That question, it really is asking this witness to speculate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the witness has already said, stated that he don't know what happened. So.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will conclude now, with the following question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Celanovic, you told us about the people you saw during those days in Bratunac. My question is, did you see Ljubomir Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Ljubomir Borovcanin from before?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have professional cooperation, did you have any social contacts with him before the 1995 events?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We had social contacts, we knew each other, we had normal communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Based on your contacts and your knowledge of Ljubomir Borovcanin, can you share with us your impression of that man?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Based on my contacts with him, my impression of him was that he was a normal, reasonable, intelligent, good man. He liked to socialise, liked to joke. He appeared as a normal, decent, good man.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: During those war years did you hear anything negative about his conduct towards other ethnicities or any crimes whatsoever?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Thank you, Mr. Celanovic. We have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I have on my list Madam Fauveau. Go ahead, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, you were talking about Muslims you had seen in the trucks, in a bus, and in a school in Bratunac. Is it right to say that you did not see that any of these people were killed in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And is it right to say that before you came to testify here in the Blagojevic case in 2004 you had never heard that one single man, that those people were not killed in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Later on I heard. It's a difficult question. I can't answer it just like that. You have to be more specific which period of time. People were killed during what period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau, both Judge Kwon and Judge Prost and myself were at the same time independently gazing at the question because obviously there was something wrong with it. Perhaps you can rephrase your question, taking also into consideration what the witness has just stated.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir before coming to testify in this case you testified in the Blagojevic case; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And this was in the month of May, 2004, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: So on the 19th of May, 2004, page 9566, the Prosecutor asked you the following question, I quote: "[In English] Did you hear anything either that evening or the next morning about bodies, 50 bodies of Muslims being found at that Vuk Karadzic school or in one of the buildings right behind it?" [Interpretation] And you have answered to that question by saying: "[In English] I didn't hear anything about that. I hear it for the first time that bodies were found either in the school or around the school." [Interpretation] My question is as follows: Is it right to say that you heard for the first time that some bodies were found at the Vuk Karadzic school or around that school, the first time you heard about it was in the month of May, 2004?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And before that date you had never heard about any bodies in Bratunac or around Bratunac on the 12th and 13th of July; is that right? My question was only concerning Bratunac, the streets of Bratunac and the school of Bratunac. I believe that there is a mistake in the translation.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat it again, your question?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, before the month of May, 2004, you had never heard that some people were killed in Bratunac in the school of Bratunac or on the streets of Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: I heard not at the school or in the streets of Bratunac, but in Kravica, and Kravica belongs to Bratunac. So I did hear, I heard that people were killed, Muslims were killed in Kravica. I heard that on the 14th or 15th of July.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, my question regards only the city of Bratunac, not the municipality of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't hear.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it exact to say that you went to Potocari when the Muslim refugees were in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Outside of Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And is it exact to say that you went to Potocari to bring Dr. Vesna Ivanovic, as well as a nurse?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And the doctor and the nurse went to Potocari in order to give medical help to refugees if that was -- if there was a need for their help; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Most likely that was the reason. What else could it be? They said that they were going there in order to provide treatment to any patients in case somebody got sick in that heat. That was the explanation they gave. I was simply asked to drive them there. They couldn't go there on foot.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And they had received the -- an order to go to Potocari; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether they received an order. Most likely they did, but at any rate they explained the reason why I needed to drive them to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it exact to say that during the war and in 1995 there were some power restrictions in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: There were, yes. There were restrictions, both in power and water-supply. Yes, it happened because the system was out of order.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it exact to say that there wasn't enough food in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And the hospital in Bratunac did not have sufficient medication; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: You put a difficult question. I heard that there was a problem with medications and that they obtained various medications through the Red Cross of Yugoslavia and from abroad and so on, which means that the supply wasn't a regular one. Now, as to just how bad shortages were, I don't know. All I know is people tried to collect medication from all sources. I know about that because I talked to doctors at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it right to say that when we talk about supplies that came from Yugoslavia that it stopped in 1994?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know when it stopped. I think that when Serbia introduced sanctions towards the Republika Srpska, then, yes, the supplies were drastically reduced. Now, as to when the sanctions were introduced, I can't remember that. The population definitely felt them, because there were shortages of everything.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it true that within your functions you could sometimes control the humanitarian convoys which were going to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: It's true in two possible situations. One was when the chief of security wasn't there, wasn't able to go, then the commander would order me to go and get paperwork. And the other situation was when security reasons required me, I would get involved and help Nikolic and military police which physically searched the vehicles. This happened if convoys were too big.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Would you agree that there were more humanitarian convoys going to Srebrenica than convoys going to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I could also add something by your leave. The same convoys arrived, but for example out of 10 trucks with food, two would go to Bratunac and eight or nine would go to Srebrenica. That's how it was. Perhaps there were some special deliveries too, I don't remember. But once they went through the check-point, usually one or two vehicles would remain in the distribution centre and the remaining vehicles, sometimes that would be up to 20, would go to Srebrenica. So there was a big difference in the number of vehicles going to Srebrenica and Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krgovic. Thank you Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Krgovic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Celanovic, I will put a couple of questions to you in relation to what you discussed with the Prosecutor, Mr. Zivanovic and Madam Fauveau. You said that you assisted in the work of investigative organs, that you collected some documents regarding war crimes and that you also participated in the inspection of convoys. As far as I could understand you, this was not part of your regular duties, the regular duties that you performed as a lawyer in the organ for legal affairs and moral guidance. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: These other tasks that the commander assigned to you in addition to your regular job duties?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you reported directly to the commander on these tasks?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You did not report to the assistant for legal affairs and moral guidance in the brigade, did you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not, because that was the arrangement with the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I have a problem with the translation. Let me repeat. You did not report to the assistant for moral guidance, but rather you reported to the commander?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Another question that I wanted to put to you. In your statement given to the security centre in Bratunac you mentioned at one point that you saw members of the Dutch battalion of UNPROFOR in Bratunac, sometime in July of 1995. Do you remember saying this in your statement?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I also remember seeing them. If it is in the statement, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, under what circumstances did you see them? Let me paraphrase your statement. It says here that you saw them in front of the military police building. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Were they armed? Did they have their personal weapons on them?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you find out the reason for them being there in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did learn about the reason. It was quite a large group. At one point I asked the military police commander about them, what was going on with them, and he said either that they had crossed over to our side, or that they had surrendered, although it's not quite logical, because they were still armed. He used this strange expression, they had crossed over to our side. That's what I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And do you know why they crossed over to your side?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Based on what he said, on what he learned from them, there was a conflict with the armed forces from Srebrenica. I'm now referring to the conflict between the forces of the international community, namely UNPROFOR, with the army from Srebrenica and that somebody got hurt, was either killed or wounded. Some of their members were killed or wounded on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not hear the last bit of the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So they took shelter?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: At any rate, they found themselves in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So they took shelter in Bratunac, you said the army, the conflict was between the members of UNPROFOR and Muslims, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Muslims, yes. But soldiers, Muslims. And he also said to me something about the interpreter saying that they were afraid of being there because they felt threatened. They felt threatened both by Muslims and Serbs, but they trusted Serbs more, so this is why they came to Serbs. They trusted us more, thinking that we wouldn't harm them. "We" meaning the Serbs, the Serbian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "up there" you mean the areas from which they had come?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the Muslim territory where this happened to them. This was in one of the villages around Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you something else. In your statement you mentioned that you heard about the attack on Srebrenica several days before it took place. Can you please tell me what did you learn about the reasons for the attack on Srebrenica? Why did the Serbian forces commence this offensive?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: It was a little bit strange. Srebrenica was under the protection of international "PRO" forces, it was a protected enclave and shouldn't have been attacked, but there were different comments and it's true actually that they carried out and I know that, carried out occasional incursions even after they were disarmed. They showed to the world that they had been disarmed, but they continued to come to our villages and attack and kill. The pretext was the burning of a village near Sekovici or Vlasenica and that a lot of people were killed, there was a lot of misfortune inflicted on that village and it was decided that they should be definitely disarmed. That was the last cause, but actually the cause was the constant incursions and the fear that this would be repeated. Not all the time, but quite frequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Were you aware, did you know about any plan that provided for the entire Muslim population to be expelled from that area?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Krgovic. Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no questions for this witness. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And that brings us back to you, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Celanovic.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you can you some of your direct testimony, but let me just clear one thing up. During the two times that you testified that you spoke with Mr. Beara on July 12th and 13th of 1995, am I correct that Mr. Beara never used or made derogatory remarks or comments against the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Not in front of me. I never heard that. He always behaved as an officer and used the appropriate terms. Maybe he used the term "enemy" or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, let me ask you -- thank you. Let me ask you this, sir: Were you ever a crime investigation inspector while you were with the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I never was an inspector, but I don't know what sort of criminal investigations you mean. It's a broad question. Could you please be more specific?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. I'll try.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: In respect of whom?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'll try. How about specifically on the 4th of March, 1993, were you ever a crime investigation inspector?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just so that I know exactly what your position was in July of 1995, can you tell me again what division or unit or station you were specifically in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't belong to any unit as such. I was simply an organ of the Bratunac Brigade command. I was a clerk for morale, religious and legal matters. That was my function.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If we can have for you, sir, with the Court's permission, and the usher's assistance, P02406 on the ELMO and the corresponding B/C/S version of that document, which I can give you the ERN number if you'd like. I said ELMO; obviously e-court, I'm sorry. Thank you. If we could have the English one on the left side of that split screen. Again it's P02406. Sir, looking at this document, I'm just going to highlight a couple of things and we will, I'm sure if you like, spend as much time as you want to because you are under oath and I want to give you the opportunity to clarify anything you have said. Do you remember, sir, this report dated the 4th of March, 1993? Do you remember it?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If we can just turn -- and I'm sorry we're going to switch just a little bit, to the fifth page of that report, both in the -- or the last page in the English and B/C/S version. Sir, on the English version there is no signature but it's obviously identified as being a document signed by you. I think that's you, Zlatan Celanovic, and do you see the B/C/S version, sir, is that your signature that appears on the last page of this document?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Am I correct then that you created this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let's go back to the first page, if you don't mind. And we will be focusing on the top portion, top left-hand portion of that page for the moment. Now, sir, looking at the top left-hand portion of the document you created and signed on or about the 4th of March, 1993, you identify yourself in the first line with your name and what position you hold, a reserve soldier, and underneath, sir, you type in specifically that you were at that time a crime investigation inspector. Correct? At least according to this report.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: That is what the war headquarters named me when I was mobilised. They said you will be doing these assignments. That's what they said. But I can explain what I actually did. I was never given an order that I was appointed to such a position.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well my question earlier to you wasn't limited to whether you were given a written, specific order. I asked you specifically, were you ever a crime investigation inspector while you were with the Bratunac Brigade. Were you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Not as an inspector, no. I would have to explain in a couple of sentences what it means to investigate. These are criminal affairs. As part of disciplinary proceedings, I compiled statements and documents which indicate that there was a discipline violation committed by the soldier. If it should turn out that on the basis of his acts he had committed a criminal act, then the same documents and the same statements would be compiled, and that's what you would name, what such a -- such work was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's change the subject and move to something else, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Next question I have, sir, as a -- whatever during your time in 1993, had you also interrogated Muslim prisoners or detainees or prisoners of war at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In early 1993, five or six people. Everything else was in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What about -- do you remember interrogating 35 of them in 1993, as reflected in your report that we have in front of us? Do you remember that? And maybe if we turn to page 3 of that corresponding report, it might help him if he needs it.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: It's not necessary. Could you please formulate the question? Not -- it's not that 35 people were interrogated in 1993, but the report was made in that year. I think the question to me was whether I had interrogated 35 people in 1993. No. That's when the report was made, and it refers to the period from the beginning of the war up to the date that the report was compiled.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. I'll take a closer look -- yes, I'll take a closer look at that, sir. Let me ask you this, sir: Have you ever been informed by the Office of the Prosecutor as to what your status is here or even when you testified in the Blagojevic case? In other words, sir, are you considered by the Prosecutor as a suspect?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And who told you that you were a suspect?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: I was told by the investigator from the Prosecutor's officer or from the Tribunal, Mr. Alastair Graham, I think it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: When did you first obtain that status, sir, as a suspect?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: I was told about the status the first time when the gentleman that I named came to my office in Bratunac to take a statement from me about the matters that I am testifying about today. I was told that according to some indications I have the status of a suspect, I was informed about my rights, and I provided a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And that was before you testified in the Blagojevic case, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And you gave that interview, sir, in December of 2003. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember the conversation, the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you a couple of questions about the Blagojevic case. You testified in that case as a defence witness, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And sir, in preparation for that case, did you assist the attorneys in the Blagojevic case with other witnesses at all in the defence of your commander, Vidoje Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't see how I could have helped them with other witnesses. I was engaged as a witness and I gave my statement. I didn't understand your question well, if you are asking something else. This is a fact that is known to the Court and to the Prosecution, that I was then a witness for the Defence. I was here in the court, and I gave a statement or I testified.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I appreciate very much, sir, you telling me if you don't understand the question, I'll try to restate it. Based upon information and belief that I have, sir, and you correct me if I'm wrong, you met with the Blagojevic defence team on numerous occasions and assisted in typing out and interviewing other potential witnesses that they may bring forth in the Blagojevic case. Is that true or false?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Partially it's true. They used my computer and internet connection. That was my help. They didn't have anywhere else to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now how many witnesses did they use your computer and your help -- and internet connection, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: They came to my place themselves, and used the internet. Since it was in English, I never turned it on, I don't know what they wrote. I didn't look. Specifically Mr. Michael Karnavas used the computer and the internet. Because they had no other place where they could have this service, so they asked me if they could use my computer and internet.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: And then they caused a lot of viruses, so they actually messed things up for me when they used my computer.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'll move along quickly. I just want to know when this approximately, sir, and how many witness did you help them out with?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. Again, I had nothing to do with other witnesses. Maybe they got a couple of names of people who potentially knew something and they contacted those people without my presence. They didn't ask for any other help. Who would be able to know? And that person would be able to know. And they searched for themselves a little bit, they had Mr. Lugonic, who was looking for those people. I gave them information and then they engaged him. The most important thing for him was my comments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think witness you don't need to give such long answers. I mean I think if you restrict your answers to a yes or no, or to a simple explanation, we'll get finished faster. Mr. Ostojic, I suppose you can move to something else as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, let me ask you this about Vidoje Blagojevic: Was he present in Bratunac during the day or days after the fall of Srebrenica in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly when I saw him after the fall of Srebrenica, but during those two, three, four to five days I definitely did not see him before or after. I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know where he was during those four or five days immediately after the fall of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know where he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you something about the Bratunac Brigade. Do you know if they were the personnel, from that brigade, that was securing or assisting in securing the Muslim detainees in the school and the stadium, as you have testified to on direct this morning -- or this afternoon?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure. I think that I saw several guards in the street next to the municipal building when I was standing on the corner at dusk. I think judging just by the uniforms that they were members of the Bratunac Brigade. I didn't go up to them, however. It's possible that it was them, I'm not sure. I couldn't mention anyone by name. I'm not saying that they were, and I'm not saying that they were not, but judging by the uniforms, they could have been members of our brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, specifically I know you mentioned the municipal building, but I'm talking about the Vuk Karadzic school where you took this walk that one day or evening. Do you remember seeing any Bratunac Brigade personnel near or around the Vuk Karadzic school, July 12th, I think you said, 1995, or 13th?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Again, about the names, let's just have it as a school, it's either Vuk Karadzic or Branko Radicevic. In any case it is the school where people were placed and I saw at dusk when I got there with Mr. Beara on the right-hand side towards the municipal building. I'm talking about the position where those people were, the school is in front to the right the street leads towards the municipal building, and next to an old building there were four to five people who, by the way they looked, seemed to be from the Bratunac Brigade, from our brigade. I didn't see them during the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And thank you for that, sir. Just so we'll clear, we will call it the school, but I want to make sure we're talking about the same school where the detainees were kept during the time immediately after the fall of Srebrenica. Whatever the name is, we can work with it by identifying it that way. How about near the stadium? Did you see any Bratunac Brigade personnel near the stadium on or about July 12th and 13th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: I really couldn't tell. I could see several soldiers standing there, just several soldiers standing there because I was at the market when I was standing there. It was too far away, and it was dark, and I really couldn't tell if they belonged to the Bratunac Brigade or not. In any case some of them were there, because I stayed at the market while Mr. Beara went up to the gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. How long were you at the market that night?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Half a minute to a minute. Until Mr. Beara came back from the gate and then we continued towards the school. Well, let's say two minutes, 50 or 60 steps that he needed to cross from there to here. Let's say it was three to five minutes. Not a very long time, not very long.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, am I correct, sir, in reading your interview and your statements that when you saw Mr. Beara on July 12th, 1995, purportedly, that he was alone, by himself, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And the next day that you saw him he was also alone, according to your interview and statements, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: He was by himself when he was talking to me. Both on the 12th and the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's all I wanted to clarify, sir. Now, do you remember, sir, when you -- prior to taking this walk purportedly with Mr. Beara that you actually went out, out of curiosity, to see what was happening in the town and you walked through the same area, the school and the stadium, before Mr. Beara arrived? Do you remember stating that in your interview or statements?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And, in fact, sir --

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And that was about 2100 hours, according to your statement, correct? Later in the evening, you went out, took a stroll to see what was happening and that's where you saw the buses and trucks, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: About 9.00, 9.30, if I say approximately; it could be an hour more or less. I can't be precise. Any time. It's when we were going, I was going during the day by myself independently.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, I want to just clarify that. According to your statement though sir, it was that you went out that night prior to meeting supposedly, Mr. Beara, prior to that, you went out at approximately 2100 hours to take a look around town, if you will. Do you remember giving that testimony or statement?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think that that's in the statement or that the statement goes like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, let's take a quick look at it. It's a minor point, but I want to make sure I'm on the same pages you. If we could look at 6D 17 on the e-court. And I'm going to -- if we could just go to page 3 of that statement. Thank you, I'm sorry. Do you have your statement here sir on e-court in front of you dated the 28th of August, 2003, and directing your attention to the second half of that statement. It starts -- and it's not identified with a specific paragraph, so therefore I can not identify the paragraph. But it states, "At around 2100 hours I went out of curiosity," and then you describe that you went up and down the street, and you went to the elementary school. Then it goes on to say that you noticed that the street was full of trucks. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And then only later in that statement, sir, actually on the next page when you -- on the lower portion of that page when you identify that you spoke with Mr. Beara and the next page you say you talked and you walked with Mr. Beara, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: The 2100 hours refers to the 12th of July, not to the 13th of July if you look up there you would see that it's referring to the 12th. When I was giving the statement I could tell what I was doing the day before, because I had been able to establish exactly what I was doing on the 13th. In the evening of the 12th, I saw those who were arriving and then the next day, too, I saw them.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And the next day would be with Mr. Beara, correct, according to you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And that would be the next day in the evening, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, in this statement here if you see, do you remember talking to the bus drivers when you went out for this curious walk and being informed by them that the Muslim detainees were going to be driven to Kladanj the next day. Do you remember that they told you that, the bus drivers?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct. They told me during the day when I went. Not in the evening, during the day. Not in the evening when I was with Mr. Beara. I never talked with anybody then. I went to take a bath and to change on the 13th, or possibly on the 12th in the evening around 9.00 that they told me, "Why are you not driving the people, how come you're standing around," and I got the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And that was on the 12th before your meeting with Mr. Beara, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: It was on the 12th at night, or on the 13th during the day. I cannot remember when it was that I asked a couple of drivers exactly what it was all about.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And the bus drivers also told you there was some sort of reorganisation, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and that they had the information about the reasons for stopping.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And, sir, Mr. Beara, that was way before you allegedly met Mr. Beara for the first time. You had this information before you met Mr. Beara, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Not much earlier. Not much before. Probably the 12th in the evening or on the 13th, around midday, was when I got the information. I mean I don't know what it states here, I don't know if dates are mentioned. Because I went twice, the evening before and then I met Mr. Beara either in the morning or in the -- in the evening or in the morning, and then on the 13th after Resid Sinanovic and the group left me, I was already tired. Nobody else came. I went home to have a quick shower and to change and that's when I went to see if anything had changed. In one of those trips to the street I had these comments with the drivers. They had information like that. I don't know who they got the information from.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, just so I understand your testimony, sir, do you remember supposedly informing Mr. Beara that the town was not secure and that you invited him to take this walk so that you could show him that the town was not secure?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think that question was put to him even in more detail earlier on, and he has answered it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If he has, I'll move on, Your Honour. I'm sorry. I didn't remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, sir, when you met with Mr. Beara that you had told him that you had this Chronicle of Our Graves and that you participated in gathering information for the book having collected eyewitness accounts of Serbs when Serb villages were destroyed and Serbian civilians killed. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm looking at your statement and if we could just turn to it, the same one that should be on the ELMO at page 4, this is what you write and I want to ask you to confirm it. Or if you want to comment on it, you can. You state -- I'll wait for it to get on, if we could have both. We're on page 4, the top portion, if we may. Is this 6D17? Yes? I don't believe the English correlates, but I can read it or we can wait, Your Honour; whatever your pleasure is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think if you can read it, that will make everybody's life easier.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I just didn't want to -- I think my learned colleague has it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It states, "He told me to use what I had and if the soldiers brought someone to the military police, it was my task to identify the persons brought in terms of whether they were suspects. He said that if any of the suspects were on the list I was to inform a security officer so that such persons --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop. Stop, Mr. Ostojic. This has been dealt with already. The question was put to him. He answered it. And it is precisely a repetition of what you are stating. I'm sure if you stop for a minute and go back to the transcript, you will find it. Or take my word for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I will obviously take your word for it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, let me ask you this: Who is Miroslav Deronjic?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Miroslav Deronjic is a politician from Bratunac. He was the president of the municipality for a while, the president of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Was he, sir, near or in the town immediately after the fall of Srebrenica in July of 1995, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember meeting him. I didn't really walk around town much. He didn't go up there. At least I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let's talk about the interview that you had with this gentleman Resid Sinanovic. Sir, I want to ask you this: Is it true that after you interviewed Mr. Sinanovic that you were not alone in your interview but another gentleman joined you in your offices to speak with Mr. Sinanovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: It's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And what's that gentleman's name? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Srbislav Davidovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And how long did -- what's his nickname, Buco?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: His nickname is not Buco, it's Buco?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How long was Mr. Davidovic with you and Mr. Sinanovic in your office with you when you were interviewing him?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: To be exactly, I spoke with Resid for about an hour, and Mr. Davidovic spoke with Resid for an hour. While he talked to him I was there for 10 to 15 minutes and then I went out so that they could speak as good old friends without my presence, and he stayed with him for about an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Who, if anyone, did you call then after your meeting to transport Mr. Sinanovic to the school?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't call anyone. The policemen went in themselves. It was a question of who were these people, the so-called specials, the two or three people. They entered the office because they knew, I informed them that he was there. You couldn't really kid around with them, they needed to know that there was another person whom Nikolic had brought in and that he was a colleague and that he wouldn't be there for long. And he wasn't there for long and they were there to take him away. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Who within the Bratunac Brigade, including your immediate superior, Major Jeftic or Mr. Blagojevic, did you inform about these two instances where prisoners were brought to you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: No one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic, how much more do you have?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: 15, 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we'll have a break now. And then we will continue afterwards. Thank you. Usual 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, we're almost done here, just a few more questions. Continuing on with Mr. Sinanovic, is it true, sir, that people from Bratunac actually visited Mr. Sinanovic when he was detained in the school?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And these people were neighbours and acquaintances of Mr. Sinanovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And these people were Stojan Ilic; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And who is other individual?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Mladoljub, I can't remember his last name right now. Krsmanovic. Mladoljub Krsmanovic, nicknamed Vampir.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. With respect to these two individuals, do you know what their ethnic -- ethnicity is?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And did you learn from them that they went to the school to visit Mr. Sinanovic after you had interviewed them?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: I learned from Stojan Ilic that the two of them had been to school.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, you came forward to the Bratunac police station, or in Republika Srpska there to give your statement on August 28th, 2003, because why?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Because I was summoned.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, isn't it accurate sir that the reason you gave your statement on the 28th of August, 2003, was because you were following the proceedings here in The Hague against Mr. Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. I simply received summons from police to appear and give statement about what I knew about Srebrenica in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you testify in any other case other than in the Blagojevic case in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, sir: With respect to Mr. Beara and the time that you met him, the first time that you claim that you met him, how did Mr. Beara leave? On foot or in a car?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: On foot. From the gate of the command to the command building, there are 50 metres. He went to the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And the second time that you claim that you saw Mr. Beara, how did he leave on the second time?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Same.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, am I correct in understanding that you decided on your own to stop interrogating the Muslim detainees in Bratunac in July of 1995, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: I had nobody else to interrogate.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But my point is though, sir, that no one told you to stop interrogating any Muslim detainees, you did it on your own, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Nobody told me anything, because there weren't any anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, how many detainees were in the school, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: I think several hundred, maybe more.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you interrogate any of those detainees?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: I did not receive instructions to go to school.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How about at the stadium, did you interrogate or interview any of the detainees in the stadium?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: I already told you that I didn't go to the stadium.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Sir, I think it was during your direct, I think you said after that second purported meeting with Mr. Beara, you never saw him again, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Not until today, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's all the questions I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ostojic. Mr. McCloskey, is there re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You said you've known Mr. Borovcanin for a long time. Is he a long-time Bratunac resident?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Isn't his family living there?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know where his family lives. But he was there two years before the Srebrenica event. That's when he was in Bratunac, two to two and a half years.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: 1993 -- the 1993 time-frame?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Roughly. 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what was his position, if any, in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: He worked in police. Whether he was the Chief of Police or commander of the station, I don't know. One of the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So he was a -- a superior in the Bratunac municipal police?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: While he was in office.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. Do you know if that was a public security or state security?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: It was police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: Civilian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, talking about that check-point that regulated the international -- the humanitarian convoys, did you have information that that check-point functioned in accordance with the orders of the Main Staff of the VRS and orders of the brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC
utterances.text: I have information that the check-point functioned in accordance of the brigade commander. Now, as to whether somebody above him issued orders, I don't know about that because he approved that check-point, and people were assigned to man it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You were asked about whether you were aware of any killings in Bratunac, and I want to ask you about the Vuk Karadzic school. Were you aware of -- do you have any information about killings at the Vuk Karadzic school in Bratunac in 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this question was already put to the witness, and the witness already answered that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm just joining, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What do you have to say about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I have prior testimony that would indicate that if perhaps he -- I could refresh his recollection, the answer might be a little different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So refer him straight away to his prior testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you remember being asked about whether you'd heard about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Another thing that Judge Prost is pointing out to me and which I had not noticed is line 20 on page 79. Bratunac in 1992. It's 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The reason I asked that question is that Ms. Fauveau asked a very broad question about killings in Bratunac and -- before he testified, and that's why I'm going back to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go straight to what you -- you want to confront the witness with.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you -- had you heard that there were killings in the Vuk Karadzic school in 1992 of Muslim detainees?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] THE FRENCH INTERPRETER: Microphone, please. Inaudible.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I will have to object on the basis that this question is not relevant in this case. It is completely outside of the frame, time-frame covered by this indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'll join also, but it is also outside the scope of the cross, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What do you have to say about this objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Throughout the defence in our case for forcible transfer the Defence has suggested that people left voluntarily or their own free will. We have heard evidence in this case that people, Muslims, left the area because of their knowledge or hearing of various events and murders that have occurred in the -- in the area of Bratunac in 1992. This particular incident was mentioned by at least one witness, and when the door is opened as wide as it was opened by the Defence, I would just prefer to bring that in. But it is of course your call.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will confer on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you have further questions, Mr. McCloskey, go ahead. But let's drop this. I think it's outside the scope of what we are discussing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I won't ask that if that's what you think. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps this is a good opportunity, given that the Prosecutor raised an issue after my cross-examination about the position of Mr. Borovcanin in Bratunac before the Srebrenica event. We can discuss with the Prosecution during which time Mr. Borovcanin was in Bratunac, and holding which post, and who -- to whom he was superior. We can stipulate this with the Prosecution and we are prepared to discuss this in order to establish whether Mr. Borovcanin was indeed employed at the police station and indeed on this post. Mr. Borovcanin came to Bratunac in August of 1992, and he left it in February of 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop. My question to you, stop -- because the witness is still present. My question to you is this: Are you in effect contesting the witness, what he stated in relation to your client? Because that you are required to do if you don't agree with what he stated. Otherwise I suggest that you -- we do not discuss any further, and we let this gentleman go.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. We don't have any problems with what the witness said. The witness said what he knew, roughly two years, which is approximately the accurate period of time, so that's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, you have come to the end of your testimony. I thank you for having come over to give testimony, and on behalf of everyone I wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, documents. You all have the list, I suppose. Are there any objections on the part of the Defence to the admission of any of these documents? We hear none. So they are all admitted as indicated in the list. There are none of them that you require to be under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Thank you. So they are so admitted. Madam Registrar will take care of registering these.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I also noticed that the defence used the statement of facts with Momir Nikolic and quite a pit of a was put on the screen. We will be offering that into evidence through Momir Nikolic and others, and if we can mark it for evidence now and perhaps put that part of it mentioned in evidence, if not the whole thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I was just on the point of asking the Defence if they wish to tender any documents. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in preparing for today's hearing we verified whether this exhibit was already admitted into evidence, since if you remember we used it during the evidence of the Deputy Commander of the Dutch battalion. It was admitted at that time, but we discussed at that time whether the whole document would be admitted or just a portion of it, and you ruled on it, Your Honours and we do not have any problems with that. And this is why we do not tender it into evidence today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I thank you for that explanation. Do you concur, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I can't -- thank you for the reminder. I don't remember that. Was the whole document in or just a portion? Because if we're getting to bigger pieces of the document, maybe we just get the whole document in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't remember myself. Anyway, any other Defence team wishes to tender any document? No. So that closes the chapter on this witness. Ms. Frease -- Ms. Gilleece.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: She is ready to go, although the Defence estimate of four hours was a little off, but that happened. So she's ready to go and we're ready to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good evening, Ms. Gilleece.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good evening, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And welcome to this Tribunal, if that's the right way to put it. You are about to start giving evidence. You know the procedure.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please proceed with the solemn declaration and then you can start testifying.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I suppose you are aware that whatever protective measures you enjoyed in the past have been lifted as per specific request by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I just want to make sure that you are content, you are happy with that arrangement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye will be putting some questions to you and we will see what happens afterwards. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good evening, Your Honours, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I will put some questions to you. I would just ask that you speak a little slowly and allow a small pause between question and answer so that we can all keep up with you. Let me start by asking you if you could just tell the Court briefly about your present employment?

utterances.speaker: EILEEN GILLEECE
utterances.text: I'm currently employed by the New Jersey state police, I am a detective sergeant with the regional intelligence centre out of west Trenton, New Jersey.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And how long have you been employed by the state police in New Jersey?

utterances.speaker: EILEEN GILLEECE
utterances.text: For 23 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And prior to -- well, not prior to that, but did you work for the office the Prosecutor at some point?

utterances.speaker: EILEEN GILLEECE
utterances.text: Yes, from 19 -- October of 1999 until April of 2003 I took an approved leave of absence from the state police and came to work at the ICTY, specifically the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And prior to your employment at the ICTY, had you been employed by the state police in New Jersey?

utterances.speaker: EILEEN GILLEECE
utterances.text: Yes, I was employed with the New Jersey state police since 1984.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: During the course of your employment, before you came to the ICTY, could you tell the Court just briefly what you -- what kind of work you did, and what kind of training you received?

utterances.speaker: EILEEN GILLEECE
utterances.text: Yes, I -- I was trained as a New Jersey state trooper, you attend an academy for six months. Everyone starts on the road, on the highway. I did that for four years, then I became a detective. I was a detective for about 11 years prior to coming to the ICTY. I investigated crimes of missing persons, paedophiles, homicide, official corruption, serious and serial crime, and organised crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Turning to your term at the Office of the Prosecutor, can you tell the Court basically what your duties and responsibilities were, beginning with your title?

utterances.speaker: EILEEN GILLEECE
utterances.text: I was an investigator for team 9. As an investigator I was charged with locating and identifying evidence, preserving it, identifying individuals with the case that I was investigating, which was a -- crimes against the Serbs -- the crimes that were committed by the ABiH during the period of 1992 to 1993 in Eastern Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, was that specific to your assignment to team 9?

utterances.speaker: EILEEN GILLEECE
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you, during the course of your work for team 9, did you have occasion to take statement from witnesses or suspects?

utterances.speaker: EILEEN GILLEECE
utterances.text: Yes, we took numerous statements from witnesses, and I met with one suspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, during the course of those activities and responsibilities, did you make use of language assistance, interpreters analysts, things of that nature?

utterances.speaker: EILEEN GILLEECE
utterances.text: Yes, we used the military analyst team quite often and always used interpreters because I only speak English.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, as a member of the investigative team with team 9, did you exchange information with other teams if there were other teams in the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: EILEEN GILLEECE
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And did you do that regularly?

utterances.speaker: EILEEN GILLEECE
utterances.text: Fairly often if it involved issues of concern for both teams.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, could I just direct your attention to the 2nd of October, 2001, if I may?

utterances.speaker: EILEEN GILLEECE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Were you working on that day for the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: EILEEN GILLEECE
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court where you were on that day?

utterances.speaker: EILEEN GILLEECE
utterances.text: I was in Serbia. I went to Valjevo Serbia to meet with 11 General Zivanovic. We met him at the -- I was a language assistant,(redacted) (redacted) from team 9 and the analyst that was assigned to team 9, Robert Cooper. The three of us went to the post office in Valjevo to meet with General Zivanovic. He then took us to a restaurant in Peti Puk, which was not too far from the post office.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, had you made a prior arrangement to meet with the general?

utterances.speaker: EILEEN GILLEECE
utterances.text: Yes, I had spoken to him on the telephone in September and he had said he would meet with us and he had some people to introduce us to that would have information concerning the -- November 6, 1992 Kamenica incident. He did not want to give me the names of the individuals I would be meeting for security purposes as we were on an unsecure phone.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, at the time that you met him, could you tell us approximately when on the 2nd of October, 2001 that occurred?

utterances.speaker: EILEEN GILLEECE
utterances.text: It was about 11.30 -- I mean 11.00 we met him at the post office and then we moved on to the restaurant at 11.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, initially when you met the general, was he alone or was he with somebody else?

utterances.speaker: EILEEN GILLEECE
utterances.text: He was alone in his own car.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And you indicated that you proceeded to follow him?

utterances.speaker: EILEEN GILLEECE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And was that to a restaurant?

utterances.speaker: EILEEN GILLEECE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, could you tell us what occurred when you arrived at the restaurant?

utterances.speaker: EILEEN GILLEECE
utterances.text: When we got to the restaurant there were two other men already seated at the table when we went in that General Zivanovic then introduced us to.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell the Court who those two men were?

utterances.speaker: EILEEN GILLEECE
utterances.text: It was Vinko Pandurevic and Djordje Sarapa.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And did General Zivanovic explain to you who they were?

utterances.speaker: EILEEN GILLEECE
utterances.text: General -- yes, he did. He told us that Pandurevic, Mr. Pandurevic had been a student of his at the military academy, and that he also was in charge of the Zvornik area when it was recaptured in 1993 in the Kamenica area. Mr. Sarapa said that he was a friend of Mr. Pandurevic's, that he was a attorney by profession, but that day in the restaurant he was merely there as a friend of Mr. Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, did there come a time when Mr. Pandurevic indicated to you that he had something to say?

utterances.speaker: EILEEN GILLEECE
utterances.text: Actually, General Zivanovic said that first he started the meeting by saying that Mr. Pandurevic wanted to tell us of his actions in 1995. I then explained to both Mr. Pandurevic and the general that team 9 investigate -- we investigated the crimes committed by the ABiH from the 1992 to 1993, however there was a team here at the Tribunal, team 6, led by Peter McCloskey, that investigates issues of that concern.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And following that explanation, did you have further occasion to speak to Mr. Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: EILEEN GILLEECE
