utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pandurevic explained that he had spoken to General Zivanovic and he was under the impression that Zivanovic trusted us and he wanted to know if it would be possible if we -- he passed us some information to team 6 because he had heard that we would listen to him without any prejudice, and he thought we would be objective and we could pass the message to Mr. McCloskey, could we do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did you agree to do that?

utterances.speaker: EILEEN GILLEECE
utterances.text: We agreed to that, I explained to Mr. Pandurevic that I was sort of on the back foot in the sense that I knew for team 9 he was not -- he was considered solely a witness. I did not know his status with the rest of the Tribunal, so I explained to him that as a witness he could speak freely to me. As a suspect to the Tribunal he had certain rights, that would be that he -- he would be allowed to have an attorney present, that he could -- anything he would say to me would be recorded and reported back to the ICTY, that he could stop speaking to me at any time. I went through all the rights as the highest standard would be for a suspect. And I gave those to him. And he agreed to speak with me. Mr. Sarapa actually thanked me for explaining the situation, and said they were quite aware of what his rights were, as did Mr. Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, it has just come to my attention, Mr. President, if it would be possible to redact the name of the interpreter who was mentioned by the witness. It is my understanding it was on page 87, line 20 of the transcript?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I have nothing to say about that, but I have something else to say at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's deal with this first. Page?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Page 87, line 20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Line 20. So we redact the last two words on that line, being the name of the language assistant. Yes, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It's been drawn to my attention that the witness is reading from something. I would like know what it is and if I haven't already got it, I would like a copy of it, please. Perhaps if she is reading from some sort of aide-memoire, we could establish the reason for her doing that but she is reading it right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Fair enough. Do you have a document in front of you that you are reading from, Ms. Gilleece?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wasn't directly reading from it sir, but yes, I have my notes to file on this incident. The number is 01848867.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's have a look at it, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I also have a memo.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It is actually marked as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's -- no, no. We would like to have a look at it first to see what it is. I can confirm that what we have here is a document which has an ERN number starting from 0184-8866 until and inclusive of 0184-8871, okay, being an investigative note to file. And then there was also a memo from Ms. Gilleece to the acting chief of investigations dated 31st of October, 2001, subject, team 9 meeting with VRS General Milenko Zivanovic, retired, Vinko Pandurevic and Djordje Sarapa, on 2nd October, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And do I understand that those documents have been marked by the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let me go through every page. Yeah, there are some minor -- there are some markings, yes, on practically every page. Not much. I suppose if -- on the other document, the memo, there is nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, this is all I require. I require, please, the date of the investigative note to file to be established, because it's an undated document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 2nd October, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: That's the date of the meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, this is the date -- investigative note to file to establish -- because it's an undated document. The date, 2nd October, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm not going to get involved in an unnecessary argument with you, but I don't belief that was the date it was created and I would like that date established, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please not overlap.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Oh, sorry. Would the Prosecution be good enough to provide a copy of the marked document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Here. Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The marked document that Mr. Haynes is referring to is -- is P02408. I believe Mr. Haynes has a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes, but I haven't got the markings, that's the point. They may be completely insignificant, but I'm entitled to them and I would like them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If the witness has made use of that document while she is testifying, I think there can be no question as to what the procedure ought to be. I think the witness, once asked, has to make this document available.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I fully agree with the Court. I'm just not sure it's established yet in the record what extent or what documents she was actually relying on if at all I would like to put that to her, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She has two statements, two documents in front of her. Perhaps she can tell us. I take it that's the whole idea is to make reference to both as it becomes necessary. Is that correct, Ms. Gilleece?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Actually, I would just need the investigative note to file. I can look at a plain one, if he doesn't want any markings. The memo was just in case anybody asked me that -- if I had any other document about that event. The one to Patrick Lopes-Terres I don't need to see; the other one would be to refresh my memory, although I'm only 45, I am having a little trouble going back to 2001, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That sounds familiar, Ms. Gilleece. At 61, it becomes a little bit more problematic. Yes, but I think we need to make it available to the parties, including yourselves, to see what annotations appear on the document. So I think you need to make a photocopy of it, or show it to Mr. Sarapa or to whoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: He can take a look at that; that would be fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's proceed, because we are running short of time. We've only got six minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. I do apologise, but I don't know where we left off at the point of the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... the problem becomes more acute. I have to check. So ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Your Honour, the simplest thing would just to get this photocopied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We just wanted --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: [Indiscernible]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So you can make an assessment, yeah. An assessment as to whether you really require it or not. You require it, we will get photocopies of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen one significant annotation that I'd like to put to the witness, so if we could have that photocopied overnight, I'm content.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You had asked the witness -- so we will make a photocopy of it, please, for everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. I think I had --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You had asked the witness whether she agreed to listen to Mr. Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And she explained that they agreed to do that. Explaining the rights that she explained to him and how Mr. Sarapa actually thanked her for explaining the situation and that both were aware of this. And then we stopped basically there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You were asked -- now it has come to my attention, Mr. President, if it would be possible to redact the name, et cetera. That's where we left it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. We have a couple minutes left, if you'd like me to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. You indicated, Ms. Gilleece that you had -- you communicated certain rights to Mr. Pandurevic and also to Mr. Sarapa. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: EILEEN GILLEECE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And can you tell us at the point that you did that, had you considered him a suspect?

utterances.speaker: EILEEN GILLEECE
utterances.text: No. Not that he was a suspect, it's just that Mr. -- General Zivanovic had told us that his Chief of Staff was Dragan Obrenovic during 1995. Mr. Obrenovic was a guest here at The Hague at the time. He also told us that he was in charge of the Zvornik area in 1995. Mr. Pandurevic to my knowledge was not on the wanted poster at the time he had very distinctive red hair and although I didn't memorise the wanted poster, he was not on it to my knowledge. I didn't recognise the name. I checked with the military analyst, Mr. Cooper was he aware of the status of Mr. Pandurevic. He said he wasn't sure of it. But just on the side of safety and for everyone's rights it would be better to -- it was better, I thought, to take the higher standard than the lower standard. This way he would be giving me anything -- any information he would be giving me would be of his own free will and I clearly wanted him to know that anything he said to me I was obligated to tell the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: During the course of your -- well, during the course of your conversation with Mr. Pandurevic, did you have occasion to reiterate these rights to him?

utterances.speaker: EILEEN GILLEECE
utterances.text: We were there from mid- -- I mean afternoon, 11.30 and we left at darkness so I guess we left at around 7.00. We ate, we spoke a lot about different things, and I probably gave him his warnings at least six to eight times during the course of the meal.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, with respect to the warnings that you gave him, did you obtain an acknowledgement or some understanding from him as to what they were and whether or not he was willing to proceed despite them?

utterances.speaker: EILEEN GILLEECE
utterances.text: Yes, he said he was fine with that, as long as I would pass the information on to Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you have in particular a conversation with Mr. Sarapa with regard to the acknowledgement of these rights?

utterances.speaker: EILEEN GILLEECE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Sarapa was very polite and very nice gentleman and said that he -- he was very polite and said -- he thanked me for giving him the warnings again each time I did and said that they were quite aware of what -- what his rights were.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, Mr. Haynes, shall we state that Mr. Sarapa is not present?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes, please. For the record it should be said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And that's quite purposeful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's why I'm raising it. Shall we stop here?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think that's a perfect point to stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Gilleece will continue tomorrow again in the afternoon but at 2.15. And we will see whether we can finish her testimony tomorrow. Thank you.
